Guyana was once a nice place to live, but had gotten very bad due to politics and crimes. The real reason some are going back is because some have retired after working two or 3 jobs in places like Queens and toronto for the past 50 years, investing and saving and where some are very successful, and with that extra money they can return, as some had always wanted to return; some had already returned even before Guyana's discovery of oil. comments.author: @allycat5892
comments.text: AI said that the street language is English. That's completely false. The language of the media, literature, schools is English, but as soon as Guyanese are at home or in the streets, they often speak Creole Patois (which can be called a dialect of English) which is based on English and some words from other languages and slangs that could be hard to understand. This Creole Patois vary from village to village, town to town. A person from Georgetown could have a hard time understanding some one from Black Bush. An example is, across the Middle East, from Palestine, to Egypt, all the way to Morocco, the language spoken in the media, schools, literature is called Modern Standard Arabic (MSA), but their street language is a dialect which has a certain amount of Arabic and lots of slangs and words from other languages which varies from one town to the next also like Guyana. A person from Morocco may have a hard time understanding some one from Lebanon.

replies.author: @allycat5892
replies.text: If you visit guyana during the Easter long weekend, then you can visit Lethem for the Rupunnuni rodeo and you can travel to Brazil, where the Brazilian border is only 5 minutes away from Lethem. You can drive to Lethem which is about 12 to 14 hours away, but to get to the Kaieteur Falls you have to fly there. There's more to see and do in Georgetown - don't get stuck in places like New Amsterdam in Berbice as there's nothing to see there and its mainly villages across Berbice. Guyana was originally built by six cultures but there's very little Portuguese left as many left Guyana decades ago due to the political problems. Very little Chinese left Many are also mixed. Depending on where you go you will see mostly descandants of India and Africa, along with Amerindians which is 10 percent of the population. On the Easter long weekend you can get into the kite flying competitions as kite flying is massive in Guyana.

replies.text: Guyana currently possesses enormous nominal wealth, but much of it exists in the form of offshore drilling infrastructure, investment costs that have not yet been fully recovered, and accumulated balances in the national fund. Converting this “revenue on paper” into tangible improvements in the living standards of individual households will require time for the oil fields to recoup their investment costs, continued progress in building basic infrastructure, and more substantive social welfare policies in the years ahead.
